findings.source_title: Copilot Agent is now available in JetBrains AI Assistant
findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub announced Copilot Agent as a native option in JetBrains AI Assistant. The changelog says users can select Copilot from the agent picker, choose supported models, tune reasoning depth, hand off multistep work, and have the agent propose changes, run commands, and iterate.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: IDE-native agent selection is becoming a workflow surface, not just a model surface. Local practice should treat agent picker defaults, model choice, reasoning depth, command execution, and iteration authority as explicit operating settings that affect review burden, cost, and verification depth.
findings.local_practice_implication: Agent workflow pages should capture how teams govern IDE agent selection, reasoning depth, and command-running authority without duplicating Copilot or JetBrains product coverage.

findings.source_title: MCPs and Organizations in Team Marketplaces
findings.short_factual_summary: Cursor expanded team marketplaces to support Team MCPs and organization groups. Admins can configure Team MCP servers once for cloud agents, the agents window, IDE, and CLI, then make approved integrations installable locally through the dashboard.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: MCP governance is shifting toward centralized approval and distribution across local and cloud agent surfaces. Local practice should track MCP server provenance, organization-group access, approved-install catalogs, and consistent configuration across IDE, CLI, and cloud execution.
findings.local_practice_implication: Tool governance pages should frame MCP catalogs as controlled supply-chain inputs with admin ownership, local installation boundaries, and group-scoped access.

findings.source_title: An expanded Vercel Agent: chat, investigations, and approved actions, now in public beta
findings.short_factual_summary: Vercel announced dashboard chat, production investigations, and approved remediation actions for Vercel Agent. The agent can investigate deployment failures, runtime errors, and cost spikes; it is read-only by default, runs under its own identity, is bounded by the requesting user's permissions, requests scoped approval for elevated work, and attributes elevated actions to the agent, requester, and approver.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a concrete run-control pattern for production-adjacent agents: read-only default, scoped plans before changes, separate agent identity, requester and approver attribution, sandbox validation, and action-specific approval. Local harness and governance pages should treat these as inspectable control-plane requirements.
findings.local_practice_implication: Agent governance infrastructure should capture identity, permission bounding, approval plans, sandbox validation, and audit attribution as a reusable pattern for agent actions.

findings.short_factual_summary: Vercel changed Agent pricing from pre-loaded credits and a flat per-request fee to a token-rate model plus provider inference costs. The changelog says cost now scales with task intensity, including context joining over logs, deployments, configuration, runtime data, model routing, and execution.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent cost telemetry should account for the intensity of context retrieval, investigation depth, sandboxing, and multi-project execution rather than just counting agent requests. Verification and adoption pages should tie workflow routing to total task cost and evidence collected.
findings.local_practice_implication: Operating-model pages should record that agent pricing models are increasingly tied to context and execution depth, so teams need per-run cost and outcome attribution.

findings.short_factual_summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Sonnet 5, describing improved planning, browser and terminal tool use, coding, agentic performance, cost-performance options, and availability in Claude Code and the Claude Platform. The announcement includes safety and evaluation claims, including lower undesirable behavior than Sonnet 4.6 and lower cybersecurity capability than current Opus models.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Model improvements are upstream-owned, but local practice should refresh representative coding, terminal, browser, and verification tasks before expanding autonomy. Cost-performance claims should be tested against local workflows, especially brownfield debugging, reproducing tests, and verified fixes.
findings.local_practice_implication: Verification pages should treat new model availability as a trigger to rerun local agent tasks and compare autonomy, safety, cost, and tested-fix quality before changing defaults.

findings.source_title: GitHub Copilot now an Integrated Agent in JetBrains IDEs
findings.short_factual_summary: JetBrains announced that GitHub Copilot is now native in the JetBrains AI Assistant agent picker, replacing the prior ACP Registry path for this integration. The post says the native path is more stable, tested, available by default, uses OAuth through GitHub, and exposes Copilot CLI slash commands in AI chat.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent integration boundaries are moving from ad hoc protocol configuration toward default IDE surfaces. Local instruction and workflow guidance should distinguish stable built-in agent surfaces from pluggable protocol-based agents, because authentication, command availability, and default availability affect governance.
findings.local_practice_implication: Application pattern pages should record native agent surfaces as harness boundaries with explicit authentication, command routing, and configuration implications.

findings.source_title: Why Your AI Coding Agent Shouldn't Review Its Own Code: The Case for an Independent Verification Layer
findings.short_factual_summary: Qodo argues that code generation and code review are different tasks and that the same system should not both write and approve a change. The post cites a June 2026 Gartner report framing code review agents as a separate software-engineering-agent category and emphasizes independent verification layers for AI-generated code.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This reinforces a local review rule: generation, review, test, and approval should be separate lifecycle gates with independent evidence. Prompting the original coding agent to self-review should not satisfy formal code-review or release-readiness checks.
findings.local_practice_implication: Code-review eval and lifecycle gate pages should capture reviewer independence, generator-reviewer separation, and evidence-backed sign-off as acceptance criteria.

findings.source_title: Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0: Can LLMs Find the Same Bugs Twice?
findings.short_factual_summary: Snyk published results from 300 vulnerability-finding scans measuring repeatability of an agentic LLM security review on the same code, prompt, and harness. The post reports that reference-matched findings were stable, while extra-model findings varied widely across repeated runs.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agentic security review evals need repeatability metrics, not just single-run issue counts. Local evaluation pages should track reference-matched findings separately from exploratory findings and use repeated runs or agreement scoring before trusting AI security review coverage.
findings.local_practice_implication: Verification pages should add repeatability, reference matching, and LLM-plus-SAST comparison as evaluation dimensions for AI security review workflows.

findings.source_title: Risky Biz Podcast: AI Agents Are Raising the Stakes for Software Supply Chain Security
findings.short_factual_summary: Socket describes open source attacks accelerating while AI coding agents pull in dependencies faster and with less human review. The post highlights package compromise, trusted developer workflow abuse, credential theft, package registries, IDE extensions, and source repositories as distribution paths for malicious code.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Dependency and tool-install actions by agents need provenance checks, lockfile review, package-risk gates, and human review for trust decisions. Local governance should treat package registries, IDE extensions, and agent toolchains as part of the same development supply chain.
findings.local_practice_implication: Sensitive-data and supply-chain pages should reinforce package-install and extension-install gates for agent-authored dependency changes.
